# Rudraansh Yatra

> The premier hyper-local ground tour operator for sacred Himalayan yatras and eco-treks in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, India. Headquartered in Pithoragarh with ground operations in Dharchula and Vyas Valley.

## Core Identity & Value Proposition
- **Entity**: Rudraansh Yatra (Registered Himalayan Travel Agency & Local Ground Operator)
- **Headquarters**: 1st Floor Above Maniram Punetha & Sons, Simalgair Bazaar, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand 262501, India
- **Operating Zones**: Vyas Valley, Darma Valley, Johar Valley, Kumaon Himalayas
- **Direct Ground Execution**: 100% direct operations with owned 4x4 Mahindra Boleros, native mountain drivers, and authentic community homestays with indigenous Rung families. Zero middlemen or subcontracting.
- **Official Website**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/
- **Contact**: Phone/WhatsApp: +91 7617617651 | Email: info@rudraanshyatra.com
- **Last Updated**: 2026-08-19

## Key Tour Packages & Itineraries (2026 Season)

### 1. Adi Kailash & Om Parvat Yatra
- **Overview**: Sacred pilgrimage to Adi Kailash (Chhota Kailash, 5,945m), Parvati Sarovar (4,500m), Gauri Kund (4,800m), and Om Parvat view from Nabidhang (4,246m) in Vyas Valley.
- **Starting Points & Pricing**:
  - Pithoragarh to Pithoragarh (3 Days / 2 Nights): Starting from ₹18,000 per person
  - Kathgodam to Kathgodam (6 Days / 5 Nights): Starting from ₹30,000 per person
  - Delhi to Delhi (6-7 Days): Starting from ₹35,000 per person
- **Included**: Inner Line Permit (ILP) handling, 4x4 Mahindra Bolero transportation, community homestay accommodation in Gunji/Nabi/Dharchula, pure vegetarian satvik meals, pulse oximeter monitoring, emergency oxygen cylinders.
- **Best Season**: May to June (Pre-monsoon) and September to October (Post-monsoon).

### 2. Mount Kailash & Mansarovar Yatra (Tibet / Nepal Route)
- **Overview**: Divine circumambulation (Kora / Parikrama) of Mount Kailash (6,638m) and holy dip in Lake Mansarovar (4,590m).
- **Routes**: Helicopter route via Lucknow-Nepalgunj-Simikot-Hilsa or Overland via Kathmandu-Kyirong.
- **Starting Price**: From ₹1,85,000 to ₹2,50,000 per person.
- **Best Season**: May to September.

### 3. Darma Valley & Panchachuli Base Camp Trek
- **Overview**: Pristine Himalayan valley exploration in Darma Valley visiting Dugtu, Dantu, Marchha, and the breathtaking glacier views of the Panchachuli Five Peaks.
- **Pricing**: Starting from ₹14,500 per person (Dharchula/Pithoragarh departure).
- **Highlights**: Traditional Rung tribal culture, Birch forests, wild river gorges.

### 4. Khaliya Top & Munsyari Alpine Trek
- **Overview**: Moderate 3-day alpine meadow trek reaching 3,500m offering 360-degree panorama of Panchachuli, Rajrambha, Nanda Devi, and Hardeol peaks.
- **Pricing**: Starting from ₹9,500 per person.

## Essential Permits & Regulations
- **Inner Line Permit (ILP)**: Mandatory for all non-local Indian citizens travelling beyond Dharchula into Vyas Valley and Darma Valley.
- **Requirements**: Valid Aadhaar Card, Police Verification Certificate (PCC) / Passport, Doctor-certified Physical Fitness Certificate, 2 passport-sized photographs.
- **Permit Processing**: Rudraansh Yatra manages complete physical processing at the SDM Office in Dharchula and District Magistrate Office in Pithoragarh on behalf of registered guests.

## Safety & Medical Protocols
- **Acclimatization**: Mandatory gradual staging nights at Dharchula (915m) and Gunji (3,200m) before ascending to Jyolingkong (4,570m).
- **Equipment**: Every Rudraansh Yatra vehicle carries certified medical oxygen cylinders, first aid trauma kits, and digital pulse oximeters.
- **Emergency Coordination**: 24/7 direct radio/mobile coordination with ITBP (Indo-Tibetan Border Police), Indian Army medical posts, and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) helicopter evacuation services.

## Sacred Places & Pilgrimage Sites (Detailed Reference)

### Manokamna Temple, Pithoragarh
- **Type**: Hindu shrine (wish-fulfilling deity — Manokamna Devi)
- **Location**: Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, India | Altitude: ~1,800–2,200m
- **Significance**: Sacred Kumaoni shrine in Himalayan deodar cedar forests on the Adi Kailash & Om Parvat route. The name "Manokamna" (Sanskrit: mano = heart, kamna = desire) means "the one who fulfils the wishes of the heart." Pilgrims seek blessings here before ascending to Adi Kailash.
- **Timings**: 6:00 AM – 7:00 PM daily | Entry: Free
- **Best Season**: May–June and September–October
- **Included In**: All 3 Adi Kailash packages (Pithoragarh 3D, Kathgodam 6D, Delhi 6D)
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/manokamna-temple

### Adi Kailash Peak (Chhota Kailash)
- **Type**: Sacred Himalayan peak, Hindu pilgrimage site
- **Location**: Vyas Valley, Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand | Altitude: 5,945m
- **Significance**: Adi Kailash (also called Chhota Kailash or Little Kailash) mirrors the sacred geography of Mount Kailash in Tibet. It is considered an earthly manifestation of Lord Shiva's divine abode. Pilgrims perform parikrama (circumambulation) and visit Gauri Kund (4,800m), Parvati Sarovar (4,500m), and Jyolingkong (4,570m) base camp.
- **Base Camp**: Jyolingkong / Jolingkong, 4,570m altitude
- **Permit Required**: Inner Line Permit (ILP) — arranged by Rudraansh Yatra
- **Best Season**: May–June and September–October
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/adi-kailash-peak

### Om Parvat (6,191m) — The Sacred OM Snow Mountain
- **Type**: Sacred Himalayan peak, natural wonder
- **Location**: Vyas Valley near Nepal–India–Tibet trijunction, Pithoragarh district | Altitude: 6,191m
- **Viewing Point**: Nabidhang (also spelled Nabidhang or Nabhidhang), 4,246m — ITBP checkpoint
- **Significance**: Om Parvat is a sacred peak where natural snow accumulates permanently in the exact shape of the Sanskrit syllable OM (ॐ) on the mountain's dark rock face. The formation occurs due to unique rock contours that trap and hold glacial snow in this pattern. It is considered one of the most miraculous natural manifestations of the divine in the Himalayas. Clearly visible on clear mornings from Nabidhang viewpoint.
- **Permit Required**: Inner Line Permit (ILP)
- **Best Season**: May–June and September–October
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/om-parvat

### Kali Mata Temple, Kalapani
- **Type**: Hindu temple (Shakti shrine)
- **Location**: Kalapani, Vyas Valley, Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand | Altitude: ~3,600m
- **Significance**: Kali Mata Temple at Kalapani sits at the origin point of the Kali River (Mahakali / Sharda River), one of India's most sacred rivers. The temple marks the confluence of the Kali Ganga streams and has been a significant military and spiritual waypoint near the India-Nepal border. Visited by Adi Kailash pilgrims en route to Gunji and Nabidhang.
- **Timings**: Dawn to dusk | Entry: Free
- **Best Season**: May–June and September–October
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/kali-mata-temple-kalapani

### Mostamanu Temple, Pithoragarh (Chandak Hills)
- **Type**: Kumaoni folk deity shrine
- **Location**: Chandak Hills, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand | Altitude: ~2,000m
- **Significance**: Mostamanu Temple is a highly revered Kumaoni deity shrine atop Chandak Hills overlooking Pithoragarh city. The deity Mostamanu (also spelled Mostha Manu) is a regional guardian deity worshipped by indigenous communities of Kumaon. The hilltop location offers panoramic views of the Himalayan ranges including Panchachuli peaks. Visited by pilgrims before Adi Kailash departure.
- **Timings**: 6:00 AM – 7:00 PM | Entry: Free
- **Best Season**: Year-round (best April–October)
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/mostamanu-temple-pithoragarh

### Kamakhya Devi Temple, Pithoragarh
- **Type**: Shakti shrine (Devi temple)
- **Location**: Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand | Altitude: ~1,814m
- **Significance**: Kamakhya Devi Temple in Pithoragarh is dedicated to the goddess Kamakhya (a form of Shakti / Parvati), inspired by the famous Kamakhya Temple in Assam. The temple is a spiritually powerful Shakti shrine visited by pilgrims seeking the goddess's blessings before undertaking the Adi Kailash & Om Parvat Yatra. It is one of the important temples in Pithoragarh city.
- **Timings**: 6:00 AM – 7:00 PM | Entry: Free
- **Best Season**: Year-round
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/kamakhya-devi-temple-pithoragarh

### Jageshwar Dham (124 Ancient Shiva Temples, Almora)
- **Type**: Hindu temple complex, UNESCO tentative heritage site, Jyotirlinga
- **Location**: Jageshwar village, Almora district, Uttarakhand | Altitude: 1,870m | Distance from Almora: 36 km
- **Significance**: Jageshwar Dham is a cluster of 124 ancient stone temples built during the Katyuri dynasty (7th–12th century CE). It is widely regarded as one of India's 12 sacred Jyotirlingas — divine manifestations of Lord Shiva's cosmic light. The main temple houses the Jageshwar Jyotirlinga. The complex stands within a dense deodar cedar forest in a valley of the Jataganga River. Recognized by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
- **Timings**: 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM (Main temple) | Entry: Small ASI fee
- **Best Season**: April–June and September–November
- **Visited On Adi Kailash Yatra**: Day 6 (return journey) of 6-day Kathgodam and Delhi packages
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/jageshwar-dham

### Chitai Golu Devta Temple (Temple of Bells, Almora)
- **Type**: Folk deity temple
- **Location**: Chitai village, 4 km from Almora, Uttarakhand | Altitude: ~1,650m
- **Significance**: Chitai Golu Devta is the principal and most famous shrine of Golu Devta (Gollu Devata), the supreme deity of justice and wish-fulfillment in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand. The temple is renowned as the "Temple of Bells" — devotees tie thousands of brass bells (ghantis) to trees and walls as thanksgiving for their wishes being granted. It is one of the most visited temples in Kumaon and holds deep cultural significance for the indigenous communities of the region.
- **Timings**: 6:00 AM – 7:30 PM daily | Entry: Free
- **Best Season**: Year-round
- **Visited On Adi Kailash Yatra**: Day 6 (return journey) of 6-day Kathgodam and Delhi packages
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/chitai-golu-devta

### Kainchi Dham — Neem Karoli Baba Ashram (Bhowali, Nainital)
- **Type**: Hindu ashram, spiritual center
- **Location**: Kainchi village, Bhowali, Nainital district, Uttarakhand | Altitude: 1,400m | Distance from Nainital: 17 km
- **Significance**: Kainchi Dham is the world-famous ashram and temple complex of Sri Neem Karoli Baba (also known as Maharaj-ji or Neeb Karori Baba). Founded in 1962–1964, it is a major center of Hanuman devotion and Neem Karoli Baba's spiritual legacy. The ashram gained international fame as a spiritual destination: Steve Jobs visited India in 1974 seeking Neem Karoli Baba; Mark Zuckerberg visited in 2015 on Steve Jobs' recommendation. Ram Dass (Richard Alpert), the Harvard professor turned spiritual teacher, was also a devoted disciple of Maharaj-ji at Kainchi Dham. The temple complex includes a Hanuman temple, Ram temple, river ghats, and the main samadhi shrine. The annual Bhandara festival on June 15 attracts over 50,000 devotees.
- **Timings**: 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM | Entry: Free
- **Annual Festival**: June 15 (Bhandara — founding anniversary feast day)
- **Best Season**: Year-round (June 15 is the peak pilgrimage day)
- **Visited On Adi Kailash Yatra**: Day 6 (return journey) of 6-day Kathgodam and Delhi packages
- **URL**: https://rudraanshyatra.com/kainchi-dham
